2.2.2.2 Hydrology, Water Quality and Aquatic Biota
Upper Reservoir
The Applicant has sponsored several studies of the physical, chemical and biological characteristics of the aquatic resources in the upper reservoir area and adjacent Howard Creek (Dysart, et al., 1973; Iseman, et al., 1975; Sigmon and Dysart, 1975; Langdon, et al., 1976; Boyne and Ingram, 1975). Figure 2-2 shows the location of sampling stations within the Howard Creek Basin. Generally, the upper sections of Howard Creek have been least disturbed and are represented by sampling stations Hll and H9 above Highway 171. West Bad Creek and Bad Creek represent tributaries in the project area and have been most recently logged (stations Wl and Bl). Lower sections of Howard Creek are represented by stations H7 through H11. Additional sampling stations were established on Limber Pole Creek and Corbin Creek near their confluence with Howard Creek (stations L2 and C1).
Hydrology
The drainage area of Jocassee Lake is 148 square miles, and the drainage area of the upper Bad Creek Project reservoir would be only 1.5 square miles. The estimated average flow of Bad Creek at the main dam site is about 5 cfs and the minimum daily average flow is about 0.6 cfs. The maximum probable flood is estimated to be 14,050 cfs. The amount of natural runoff from the upper reservoir basin is insignificant compared to the total volume of water which would be recycled during the operation of the project, and has therefore not been considered in power operation studies. The total water requirements of the project would be supplied by pumping from Jocassee Reservoir.
Flow relationships within the Howard Creek Basin were calculated by comparing the measured flows on those dates from 1973 to 1975 for which data were available at stations H1, H7, B1, W1, and H9. Figure 2-3 shows the percentage of the flow in Howard Creek contributed by Bad Creek and West Bad Creek. About 48 percent of the flow (26 to 67 percent) in Howard Creek immediately below the confluence with Bad Creek is contributed by Bad Creek and West Bad Creek, while at station H1 near Lake Jocassee about 17 percent of the flow (12 to 21 percent) is contributed by these tributaries. Flow in lower Howard Creek is increased by the contributions from Limber Pole and Corbin Creeks plus local inflows.
